raw_response:
I'm 76 now, and my legs aren't what they used to be. Forty years I've been working these 10 mu and a bit of land in Quzhou, and I've seen good years and bad years. My son and his wife are here too, and the grandchildren help when they're not in school, so we have hands, but I still need to think careful about every yuan we spend.

**Wheat** — I always plant wheat in mid-October, around the 15th or so, when the soil is still warm enough. I use the same improved variety I've been using for several years now. Last year I tried to save a bit on seed and the stand was thin, so this year I'll buy fresh seed, about 15 jin per mu. That costs me maybe 45 yuan per mu, but it's worth it.

For fertilizer, I usually put down about one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that's my base. Then when the wheat turns green in spring, if it looks yellow and hungry, I topdress with urea, maybe another half bag per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang used less last year and his wheat was shorter than mine, so I'm not cutting back. Altogether that's about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, maybe a bit more. I don't have soil tests — I just look at the color of the wheat and remember what worked before.

Irrigation — I have the well, but pumping costs electricity money. Three times for wheat: once after planting to help it settle, once at jointing in spring when it's growing fast, and once at filling if the spring is dry. Four times is too expensive, twice might not be enough if it's a dry spring like two years ago. I'll stick with three.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide once in early spring when the weeds are small. For insects, I only spray if I see them. Last year there were aphids, so I'll keep an eye out.

**Maize** — Planting in mid-June is the hardest week of the year. Wheat comes off, and maize has to go in almost immediately. My son drives the tractor now, and we hire the thresher from the village. I plant hybrid maize seed, about 3 jin per mu, costs around 50 yuan per mu. 

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer down at planting, about the same as wheat — one bag per mu. Then I topdress with urea at the big trumpet leaf stage, about half a bag. Total nitrogen around 14 kg per mu. I don't like to put it all at once because if there's a big rain it washes away.

Maize irrigation — maybe twice. Once right after planting if it's hot and dry, and once at tasseling if there's no rain. Some years I don't irrigate maize at all if the summer rains are good, but lately the summers have been patchy, so I'll plan for two times.

Pesticide for maize — definitely herbicide at planting, and I watch for corn borers. The seed dealer has some coated seed that helps, so I'll get that.

**Labor and costs** — My family does most of the work: planting, fertilizing by hand, spraying. We hire a combine for wheat harvest and maybe hire two or three day-laborers for maize harvest if the children are busy. At my age I supervise and do the lighter jobs. I keep about 3,500 yuan cash ready for inputs this year. I can't spend more than that — we need money for medicine and the grandchildren's school things.
